# Backbone of the meta-analysis map (generated by spec/build_map.py; do not edit)

Edit the data in `spec/build_map.py` and run it again. The full tree is in `spec/tree.md` and `spec/map.html`.

Status: OK = confirmed from the source and in taxonomy v11. NEW = confirmed or proposed, not in v11. CHECK = not yet confirmed from a primary source.

Counts: pathways in total 564; interventional 454; interventional, in v11's scope 214; of those, confirmed 185; new, not in v11 350; still to check 99; status runnable 0; status planned 404; status specified 61; status to_check 99.

## Notes on frameworks, groups and datatypes

| Tier | Node | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| framework | 1. Interventional (effect of an intervention) | Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions. One-group analyses pool a proportion, a mean or an incidence rate from single groups. | CH-10, MF-escalc |
| framework | 2. Diagnostic test accuracy | Not in v11. The Cochrane diagnostic accuracy handbook could not be read online, so most entries are unverified. | DTA-HB, MADA |
| framework | 3. Prognosis | Not in v11. Prediction model entries are confirmed from the metamisc documentation; prognostic factor entries are unverified. | VALMETA, RILEY |
| framework | 4. Association | Not in v11 (correlation was excluded there). | MF-escalc, DOSRES |
| framework | 5. Measurement reliability | Not in v11. Supported by metafor. | MF-escalc |
| group | Change or matched pairs (same people measured twice) | Not in v11. Needed for before-and-after designs, and for crossover trials (Cochrane 23.2). | CH-23 s23.2, MF-escalc |
| group | Multiple groups (network) | Both common-effect and random-effects models are available. Before fitting, judge transitivity: whether effect modifiers are similar across the comparisons. After fitting, check consistency and rank the treatments (P-score, SUCRA, rankogram); rankings are outputs, not metrics. | CH-11 s11.2.2, s11.4.4, s11.6.4, NM, NM-man, MD-senn, DMA |
| datatype | Individual participant data | Two-stage analysis: analyse each study, then pool the estimates through the Precomputed estimate branch. One-stage analysis is shown here. | CH-26 s26.4.2, s26.4.5 |

## Methods

| Method | Function | Models | Reads | Analysis types | Source | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inverse variance | `metafor::rma.uni()` | Common effect, Random effects | arm, est | standard, subgroup, meta-regression, cumulative, leave-one-out | MF-uni, CH-10 | OK | Random effects: 12 estimators of the between-study variance (REML is the default); Hartung-Knapp interval available (test="knha"). Cumulative and leave-one-out need a model without moderators. |
| Mantel-Haenszel | `metafor::rma.mh()` | Common effect | arm | standard, cumulative, leave-one-out | MF-mh, CH-10 | OK | No moderators. Generally preferred to inverse variance for common-effect binary analyses (Cochrane 10.4.1). |
| Peto | `metafor::rma.peto()` | Common effect | arm | standard, cumulative, leave-one-out | MF-peto, CH-10 | OK | For rare events, balanced arms and small effects. Not a default (Cochrane 10.4.2). |
| Generalized linear mixed model | `metafor::rma.glmm()` | Common effect, Random effects | arm | standard, subgroup, meta-regression | MF-glmm | OK | Common effect is method="EE"; random effects uses maximum likelihood only. RR and RD are experimental. No cumulative or leave-one-out function. |
| Penalised logistic regression (rare events) | `meta::metabin(method="LRP")` | Common effect, Random effects | arm | standard | META-bin | NEW, CHECK | Handles single and double zero studies without a continuity correction. Which models it fits is not confirmed. |
| Bayesian normal-normal hierarchical model | `bayesmeta::bayesmeta()` | Random effects | arm, est | standard, subgroup, meta-regression | BM, BM-bmr | OK | No MCMC. Meta-regression and subgroups through bmr(). No cumulative or leave-one-out function found in the manual. |
| Multilevel / multivariate | `metafor::rma.mv() with vcalc()` | Common effect, Random effects | arm, est | standard, subgroup, meta-regression | MF-mv | OK | For studies that contribute several dependent estimates. Without a random term it fits a fixed-effects model (v11 says random only). REML or ML. No Hartung-Knapp, cumulative or leave-one-out function. |
| Observed minus expected and variance (log-rank / Peto) | `computed as (O-E)/V with variance 1/V` | Common effect | oev | standard | CH-10 | NEW, CHECK | Cochrane 10.9: only fixed-effect methods in RevMan. R implementation not chosen yet. |
| One-stage regression on participant data (pairwise) | `mixed-effects or multilevel regression` | Random effects | ipd | standard, subgroup, meta-regression | CH-26 | CHECK | Stratify by study (Cochrane 26.4.2, 26.4.5). R packages still to confirm. |
| Frequentist, graph-theoretical | `netmeta::netmeta()` | Common effect, Random effects | arm, est | standard | NM, CH-11, DMA | NEW | Arm-level data go through pairwise(). Between-study variance: DL, REML or ML. Does not support meta-regression. |
| Frequentist, multivariate | `metafor::rma.mv()` | Common effect, Random effects | arm, est | standard, subgroup, meta-regression | MD-senn, MF-mv | OK | Arm-based or contrast-based. The documented example fits both a fixed-effects and a random-effects network model. |
| Mantel-Haenszel for networks (sparse binary data) | `netmeta::netmetabin()` | Common effect | arm | standard | NM-bin | NEW | Methods MH and NCH are common-effect only. |
| Bayesian hierarchical (MCMC) | `gemtc with JAGS` | Common effect, Random effects | arm, est | standard, meta-regression | DMA, CH-11 | CHECK | Supports meta-regression. Common-effect option not confirmed from the manual. |
| One-stage regression on participant data (network) | `mixed-effects regression, frequentist or Bayesian` | Random effects | ipd | standard | CH-26 | CHECK |  |
| Bivariate model (Reitsma) | `mada::reitsma()` | Random effects | tab | standard, subgroup, meta-regression | MADA | OK | Estimation: reml (default), ml, mm, vc, or fixed. Equivalent to the HSROC model when there are no covariates. |
| Hierarchical summary ROC model (Rutter and Gatsonis) | `implementation not chosen` | Random effects | tab | standard, subgroup, meta-regression | DTA-HB, MADA | CHECK | Used when studies apply different thresholds. |
| Univariate pooling | `mada::madauni()` | Common effect, Random effects | tab | standard | DTA-HB | CHECK | Ignores the correlation between sensitivity and specificity. |
| Meta-analysis of prediction model performance | `metamisc::valmeta()` | Common effect, Random effects | est | standard | VALMETA, DEBRAY | OK | REML by default, Hartung-Knapp interval, prediction interval; Bayesian option. |
| Dose-response meta-analysis | `dosresmeta::dosresmeta()` | Common effect, Random effects | dose | standard | DOSRES | OK | One-stage or two-stage. Covariance by Greenland-Longnecker or Hamling. Linear or non-linear trend. |

Reads: arm = arm-level summary data, est = precomputed estimates, ipd = participant data, oev = O - E and V, tab = diagnostic 2x2 tables, dose = estimates by dose level.

## Rules

| # | Rule | Compared with v11 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Inverse variance works with every metric, both models, and both arm-level and precomputed data. | agrees | MF-uni, CH-10 s10.3 |
| R2 | A precomputed estimate can only be pooled by methods that take an estimate and its variance: inverse variance, bayesmeta, rma.mv. | agrees | MF-mh, MF-peto, MF-glmm |
| R3 | Mantel-Haenszel needs arm-level counts and gives OR, RR, RD (2x2 tables) or IRR, IRD (person-time). Common effect only. | agrees | MF-mh |
| R4 | "Random-effects Mantel-Haenszel" is not a separate method: the random-effects estimate uses inverse-variance weights. | agrees | META-bin |
| R5 | Peto needs 2x2 tables and gives only the Peto odds ratio. Common effect only. For rare events, balanced arms, small effects. | agrees | MF-peto, CH-10 s10.4.2, s10.4.4.3 |
| R6 | GLMM gives OR (2x2), IRR (two-group counts), logit proportion and log rate. RR and RD are experimental. | v11 wrong: lists OR, RR, RD | MF-glmm |
| R7 | GLMM random effects uses maximum likelihood only. | v11 wrong: says REML, ML, EB | MF-glmm |
| R8 | GLMM does not apply to continuous outcomes. | agrees | MF-glmm |
| R9 | For rare events avoid inverse variance, including DerSimonian-Laird. | missing in v11 | CH-10 s10.4.4.3 |
| R10 | Subgroup analysis and meta-regression need moderators: available in rma.uni, rma.glmm, rma.mv and bayesmeta (bmr); not in rma.mh or rma.peto. | agrees; answers v11's open question on bayesmeta | MF-uni, MF-glmm, MF-mv, BM-bmr |
| R11 | Cumulative and leave-one-out functions exist for rma.uni, rma.mh and rma.peto only. | v11 wrong for GLMM and rma.mv | MF-cumul, MF-l1o |
| R12 | Cumulative and leave-one-out need a model without moderators. | missing in v11 | MF-cumul, MF-l1o |
| R13 | bayesmeta has no cumulative or leave-one-out function in the part of the manual read. It needs no MCMC. | answers v11's open question | BM |
| R14 | Hartung-Knapp intervals apply to rma.uni random-effects models only. | agrees | MF-uni, MF-mv |
| R15 | REML is the default in metafor and RevMan. Cochrane also cites Paule-Mandel and says no estimator is universally preferable. | v11 overstates: calls REML Cochrane's preference | CH-10 s10.10.4.4 |
| R16 | Network meta-analysis can use a common-effect or a random-effects model. Chapter 11 never mentions excluding the common-effect model; netmeta and the rma.mv example fit both. | v11 wrong: excludes fixed effect | CH-11, NM, MD-senn |
| R17 | P-score and SUCRA are rankings computed after a network model is fitted. They are outputs, not effect measures. | v11 wrong: lists them as metrics | NM-man, CH-11 s11.6.4, DMA |
| R18 | A network analysis must check transitivity and consistency (node-splitting, design decomposition, net heat plot). | missing in v11 | CH-11 s11.2.2, s11.4.4 |
| R19 | Networks usually assume one common between-study variance across comparisons. | missing in v11 | CH-11 s11.4.3.2 |
| R20 | Mantel-Haenszel for networks (netmetabin) is common-effect only. | missing in v11 | NM-bin |
| R21 | IPD: two-stage analysis joins the precomputed pathway. One-stage analysis needs a mixed-effects regression stratified by study. | agrees | CH-26 s26.4.2, s26.4.5 |
| R22 | Cluster-randomized trial: divide the sample size (and events) by the design effect 1 + (M - 1) x ICC, or multiply the SE by its square root. | agrees | CH-23 s23.1.4-23.1.6 |
| R23 | Crossover trial: use a paired analysis; without paired data, impute the SD of differences from an assumed correlation. | v11 wrong: applies the cluster formula | CH-23 s23.2.5-23.2.7 |
| R24 | Study with three or more arms in a pairwise analysis: combine arms (recommended in most situations), model the correlation, or use a network. Choosing one pair, or splitting the shared group, is not generally recommended. | missing in v11 | CH-23 s23.3.4 |
| R25 | Time-to-event from O - E and V: RevMan offers fixed-effect methods only, and this map follows it; log hazard ratios with SEs are pooled by inverse variance. | missing in v11 | CH-10 s10.9 |
| R26 | Diagnostic accuracy: sensitivity and specificity are pooled jointly (bivariate model); the HSROC model is equivalent without covariates. | not in v11 | MADA |
| R27 | Prediction model performance: pool the c-statistic on the logit scale and O:E on the log scale, random effects with Hartung-Knapp and a prediction interval. | not in v11 | VALMETA |
| R28 | Tests for funnel plot asymmetry need at least 10 studies; Egger's original test is not recommended for odds ratios or SMDs. | not in v11 | CH-13 s13.3.4.4 |
| R29 | Trim and fill and selection models work on rma.uni models only (trim and fill: no moderators). | not in v11 | MF-trimfill, MF-selmodel |
| R30 | Meta-regression is generally not advised with fewer than ten studies. | missing in v11 | CH-10 s10.11.4 |
| R31 | A network's standardized mean difference is Cohen's d. From arm-level data, pairwise() computes it that way for netmeta, since the small-sample correction of Hedges' g would make a multi-arm study's comparisons disagree; contrast-level estimates should be Cohen's d for the same reason. The map offers one network SMD. | v11 wrong: offers d and g separately for rma.mv and gemtc networks | META-pw |
| R32 | In this map, the Peto odds ratio is offered only with Peto's method. Cochrane presents it as the estimate Peto's method computes: an approximate log odds ratio from observed minus expected events and their variance. escalc(measure="PETO") also computes it study by study; this map doesn't offer pooling it with another method. | agrees | CH-10 s10.4.2, MF-escalc |

## Method and metric pairs still to check

Each method and metric here is confirmed on its own; their pairing is not yet, so its pathways are to check.

| Method | Metric | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Frequentist, multivariate | Standardized mean difference (Cohen's d) | R31's source covers netmeta; how rma.mv networks take an SMD is still to read in metafor's documentation |
| Bayesian hierarchical (MCMC) | Standardized mean difference (Cohen's d) | R31's source covers netmeta; gemtc's measures are still to confirm (issue #40) |

## Sections that apply across the tree

| Section | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Analysis types | standard, subgroup, meta-regression, cumulative, leave-one-out, sensitivity. What each method supports is listed on the method. | CH-10 s10.11, s10.14 |
| Heterogeneity outputs | Between-study variance, I-squared, Q test, prediction interval (encouraged with about five or more studies). | CH-10 s10.10 |
| Small-study effects and missing results | Funnel plot, regression test (regtest), trim and fill (trimfill), selection models (selmodel). | CH-13, MF-regtest, MF-trimfill, MF-selmodel |
| Unit-of-analysis corrections | Cluster trials, crossover trials, studies with several arms, repeated measurements. | CH-6 s6.2, CH-23 |
| Network outputs | Ranking (P-score, SUCRA, rankogram), league table, consistency checks. | NM-man, CH-11 |

## Still to check

1. Read the Cochrane diagnostic accuracy handbook, Ch. 9 and 10 (needs a Cochrane account) and confirm the diagnostic branch.
2. Read Riley et al. 2019 and Debray et al. 2017 in full and confirm the prognosis branch.
3. Read Cochrane Ch. 24 (non-randomized studies) for the exposure-outcome branch.
4. Choose the R implementation for the HSROC model and for O - E and V data.
5. Confirm R packages for one-stage IPD, pairwise and network.
6. Confirm the common-effect option and inputs of the Bayesian network engine (gemtc).
7. Confirm from metafor's and gemtc's documentation how their networks take a standardized mean difference (Cohen's d, R31).
8. Confirm which models penalised logistic regression (metabin LRP) fits.
9. Read the rest of the bayesmeta manual.
10. Record the Handbook version and the date of each chapter.
11. Decide whether to offer refit loops for cumulative and leave-one-out where the package has no function.
